title: Episode 264: 🇦🇺 Aphantasia, Anendophasia & the Future with Kevlin Henney

sentences.en: Technoautism still exists, but I want to say that it was more of a default.
sentences.zh: 技术自闭症依然存在，但我认为它更像是一种默认状态。

sentences.en: It was the idea that the future means progress.
sentences.zh: 这就是未来意味着进步的观点。

sentences.en: The 21st century is somehow, if we can just get past this small issue of maybe wiping ourselves out, if we can get past that, then the 21st century, maybe we grow up.
sentences.zh: 21世纪不知怎么的——如果我们能闯过自我毁灭这个小关卡的话，如果我们能闯过去的话——那么在21世纪，也许我们会真正成熟起来。

sentences.en: It's a kind of a Star Trek universe.
sentences.zh: 这有点像《星际迷航》的宇宙。

sentences.en: It's like we get to a point and all of the potential is unleashed, all of these possibilities.
sentences.zh: 就像我们达到了某个临界点，所有的潜能都被释放了，所有的可能性都被激活了。

sentences.en: And this is not just sort of saying, you know, flying cars and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 这可不仅仅是在说，你知道的，会飞的汽车之类的事情。

sentences.en: It's much deeper in terms of thinking about utopias and along those lines.
sentences.zh: 在思考乌托邦以及诸如此类的话题时，它要深刻得多。

sentences.en: And there was genuinely a sense in the 70s and 80s, I can't speak for the 60s, I was not really there, only vaguely present.
sentences.zh: 而且在70年代和80年代，确实有一种这样的氛围——我没法代表60年代，因为我当时并不在那儿，只有极其模糊的记忆。

sentences.en: But 50s and 60s, you know, the Jetson view of the future, and you just see it in the science fiction of the time.
sentences.zh: 但在50和60年代，你知道的，杰特逊式的未来愿景，你在当年的科幻作品里到处都能看到。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 264, recorded on December 11th, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 264 期，本期节目于 2025 年 12 月 11 日录制。

sentences.en: My name is Conor, and today I chat with Kevlin Henney, live from YOW 2025 in Sydney, Australia.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我和凯夫林·亨尼在澳大利亚悉尼的 YOW 2025 现场进行交谈。

sentences.en: We chat about aphantasia, anendophasia, synesthesia, techno-optimism, the future, and more.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了聊心盲症、无内语症、联觉、技术乐观主义、未来等等话题。

sentences.en: We are here.
sentences.zh: 我们到这里了。

sentences.en: I actually don't remember what episode this will be.
sentences.zh: 我其实记不清这是第几期节目了。

sentences.en: I think it's episode 264.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是第 264 期。

sentences.en: The last time you heard from us, folks, it was October 10th.
sentences.zh: 各位，大家上次听到我们的声音，还是在 10 月 10 日。

sentences.en: We've been releasing episodes for weeks now, and it is now December 11th, soon to be released on December 12th.
sentences.zh: 我们已经连续几周发布节目了，而现在已经是 12 月 11 日，很快就会在 12 月 12 日发布。

sentences.en: So you went from very stale audio or recordings to now fresh.
sentences.zh: 所以你们听到的内容从非常陈旧的音频或录音，变成了现在的全新内容。

sentences.en: And we're here with four-time guests, I think.
sentences.zh: 我们迎来了第四次做客的嘉宾，我想是的。

sentences.en: We cut your last episode into four parts with Kevlin Henney.
sentences.zh: 我们把你和凯夫林·亨尼合作的上一期节目剪成了四部分。

sentences.en: And we just both finished speaking for what was the third installation of three different conferences.
sentences.zh: 我们俩刚刚结束了三个不同会议中的第三场演讲。

sentences.en: We were at YOW 2025.
sentences.zh: 我们参加了 YOW 2025。

sentences.en: We were first in Melbourne, then we were in Brisbane, or as I've been told, Brizzy, is how they call it.
sentences.zh: 我们先去了墨尔本，然后去了布里斯班，或者像别人告诉我那样，他们叫它“布里兹”（Brizzy）。

sentences.en: And now we are in Sydney.
sentences.zh: 现在我们在悉尼。

sentences.en: And we're going to talk.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊一聊。

sentences.en: I mean, for folks that haven't listened to your first four-part episode, and that might not be familiar, I mean, I can introduce a little bit one of my favorite speakers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对于那些没有听过你那期四部分节目的朋友们，如果他们可能不太熟悉，我可以稍微介绍一下我最喜欢的演讲者之一。

sentences.en: I just had, I've been reminded that you are the author of several books, including my favorite, 97 Things Every Programmer Should Know and Every Java Programmer Should Know.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚想起来，你是好几本书的作者，包括我最喜欢的《程序员的职业素养》（97 Things Every Programmer Should Know）以及《Java程序员的职业素养》。

sentences.en: And I think there, I know there's a couple of the 97 books.
sentences.zh: 我想还有，我知道“97”系列还有好几本。

sentences.en: I don't know if you're co-authors on those ones.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是不是其中几本的共同作者。

sentences.en: I don't think so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想不是的，是的。

sentences.en: But a veteran of the speaking track, and we're going to talk about maybe the talk that you gave at this conference, and also in NDC, and I think at a different conference.
sentences.zh: 不过你是一位身经百战的演讲者，我们接下来要聊聊你在这次会议上做的演讲，还有在 NDC，以及我想在另一个会议上的演讲。

sentences.en: But also, we're going to have to talk about the talk that you gave at GoToCopenhagen.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还不得不聊聊你在 GoTo 哥本哈根大会上的演讲。

sentences.en: But anyways, before we get into that, and we're going to have to talk about Aphantasia a little bit, because we've been chatting about that.
sentences.zh: 不过无论如何，在我们深入探讨之前——而且我们还得稍微聊聊心盲症，因为我们一直在聊这个。

sentences.en: But before we get to that, maybe I'll hand the mic to you, and you can color in the bio bits that I missed, just in case we had new listeners since the last time you were on.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，也许我把话筒交给你，由你来补充我漏掉的个人简介部分，以防自从你上次来节目之后我们有了新听众。

sentences.en: Okay, so, yeah, I edited a bunch of books.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以，是的，我编辑过一堆书。

sentences.en: I contributed to the 97 Things series, pattern-oriented software architecture books as well.
sentences.zh: 我参与了“97 Things”系列丛书的编写，还有面向模式的软件架构系列图书。

sentences.en: I've been a columnist, a blogger, and all kinds of bits and pieces.
sentences.zh: 我当过专栏作家、博主，写过各种各样的文章和杂文。

sentences.en: And occasionally can be found running workshops and doing various bits and pieces for people.
sentences.zh: 偶尔还能看到我在举办工作坊，为人们做各种各样的活动。

sentences.en: I guess that's it.
sentences.zh: 我想就是这样吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can normally run into me either somewhere on the internet or at a conference.
sentences.zh: 是的，你通常要么能在互联网的某个地方碰到我，要么在会议上见到我。

sentences.en: And, yeah, fantastic.
sentences.zh: 而且，太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, like I said, one of my top three speakers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，就像我说的，我心目中的前三名演讲者之一。

sentences.en: And I think, I don't know, I actually, off the top of my head, I don't know if I can rank.
sentences.zh: 我想，我不知道，其实凭我的第一直觉，我不知道自己能不能排出个高下。

sentences.en: But if I had to choose one, and you've probably heard me say this, but you might have forgotten.
sentences.zh: 但如果我必须选一个——你可能听我说过这话，但也可能忘了。

sentences.en: Declarative Thinking, Declarative Practice.
sentences.zh: 《声明式思维，声明式实践》（Declarative Thinking, Declarative Practice）。

sentences.en: Is that the title?
sentences.zh: 是这个标题吗？

sentences.en: So, this was a talk.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一场演讲。

sentences.en: Now, it's got to be given at least six, seven years plus ago.
sentences.zh: 现在算来，它至少是六、七年前甚至更久以前做的了。

sentences.en: Because this was one of the first talks that I watched when I started watching online talks.
sentences.zh: 因为这是我开始观看线上演讲时看的第一批演讲之一。

sentences.en: And it's a link in the show notes, folks.
sentences.zh: 节目shownotes里会有链接，各位。

sentences.en: We'll link all the talks, but it's a great talk.
sentences.zh: 我们会把所有的演讲链接都放上去，但这真的是一场很棒的演讲。

sentences.en: So, where should we start?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: Should we start with aphantasia, synesthesia, or should we start with the go-to Copenhagen talk?
sentences.zh: 我们应该从心盲症、联觉开始，还是从哥本哈根 GoTo 大会的演讲开始？

sentences.en: Or should we start with, yeah, what should we start with?
sentences.zh: 或者我们应该从……是的，我们该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: Okay, let's talk about the feely stuff, first of all.
sentences.zh: 好吧，首先我们来聊聊那些走心的话题。

sentences.en: So, we've been talking, so the conversations that have been going on have been very much about how we sense the world differently, how we experience the world differently.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论，最近的这些对话很大程度上都围绕着我们如何以不同的方式去感知世界，如何以不同的方式体验世界。

sentences.en: And it's come up in the context.
sentences.zh: 这在一些语境下被提了出来。

sentences.en: It turns out that I am colorblind, and so is Kent Beck, who is one of the other keynote speakers here.
sentences.zh: 原来我是色盲，这里另一位主题演讲嘉宾肯特·贝克（Kent Beck）也是。

sentences.en: And technically, we're both red-green colorblind, but we actually have different versions of colorblindness.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，我们俩都是红绿色盲，但我们的色盲类型其实有所不同。

sentences.en: In terms of who perceives red, who perceives green.
sentences.zh: 就谁能感知红色、谁能感知绿色而言。

sentences.en: But in addition to being colorblind, I'm also synesthetic.
sentences.zh: 但除了色盲之外，我还有联觉（synesthetic）。

sentences.en: And synesthetic means you have cross-sensory wiring.
sentences.zh: 联觉意味着你的跨感官神经是连在一起的。

sentences.en: And in a lot of people, the typical one, and one that I have, is fairly run-of-the-mill, is that I associate colors with digits, digits and letters.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，最典型的一种——也是我所拥有的一种——相当平淡无奇，那就是我把颜色和数字、数字与字母联系在一起。

sentences.en: So, therefore, when I think of a number, it also has color associations.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我想到一个数字时，它也自带颜色的联想。

sentences.en: When I think of a word, it has color associations.
sentences.zh: 当我想到一个词时，它也有颜色的联想。

sentences.en: It helps me remember my hotel room and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这能帮我记住我的酒店房间号之类的事情。

sentences.en: What's my room number?
sentences.zh: 我的房间号是多少？

sentences.en: And so you get some weird cross-wiring like that.
sentences.zh: 所以你会得到一些诸如此类奇异的感官交织。

sentences.en: But then you get this weird stuff that the conversations have gone off in terms of how unique a person's experience to the world is.
sentences.zh: 但随后你还会发现一些奇特的现象，正如我们在对话中探讨的那样，个人的世界体验是多么的独特。

sentences.en: And that we make a number of assumptions about how other people perceive the world.
sentences.zh: 我们对其他人如何感知世界做出了许多假设。

sentences.en: Normally, it's based on our own experience.
sentences.zh: 通常，这是基于我们自身的经验。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of things that we share culturally.
sentences.zh: 我们在文化上有很多共享的东西。

sentences.en: So, common experiences that we have is how we hear things and how we taste things, you know.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们共同的经验包括我们如何听到声音以及我们如何品尝食物，你知道的。

sentences.en: And we know about other people's tastes.
sentences.zh: 我们了解别人的口味。

sentences.en: They do like this flavor.
sentences.zh: 他们确实喜欢这种风味。

sentences.en: They don't like that flavor.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢那种风味。

sentences.en: They hate strawberries.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌草莓。

sentences.en: Coriander tastes like soap to them.
sentences.zh: 香菜对他们来说尝起来像肥皂。

sentences.en: These are things that we talk about.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们经常讨论的事情。

sentences.en: And then we have these things that we don't talk about because they don't really come up in conversation much and that we make assumptions about.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些我们不常讨论的事情，因为它们在对话中很少被提及，而我们却对它们想当然地做出了假设。

sentences.en: And one of them, I didn't realize I was synesthetic until I was in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是，我直到二十多岁才意识到自己有联觉。

sentences.en: Didn't even know there was a word for it.
sentences.zh: 甚至连这个词都不知道。

sentences.en: These days, it's a lot easier to find these things out.
sentences.zh: 如今，要发现这些事情要容易得多了。

sentences.en: But you also have it in terms of other neurodiversity, in terms of ADHD, autism, all across the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 但你在其他神经多样性方面也能看到这一点，比如多动症（ADHD）、自闭症，涵盖了整个谱系。

sentences.en: And then you get some really interesting ones, which are not addition of things, but the absence of things.
sentences.zh: 然后你会遇到一些非常有趣的情况，它们不是某种感官的增加，而是感官的缺失。

sentences.en: And aphantasia is an interesting one because it's basically the absence of a mind's eye that you don't have a visualization of what you're reading, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 心盲症（aphantasia）就是一个很有意思的例子，因为它基本上意味着“心灵之眼”的缺失，也许你在阅读时不会产生可视化画面。

sentences.en: You know, when you're reading a book, do you visualize the characters?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你读一本书时，你会把里面的角色可视化吗？

sentences.en: And there is a, it turns out that not everybody does.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，并不是每个人都会。

sentences.en: And this is a surprise to many people.
sentences.zh: 这让许多人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: In fact, the term itself, aphantasia, is only really about 10 years old or so.
sentences.zh: 事实上，“心盲症”这个词本身大概也就是最近十年的事。

sentences.en: Even though people started becoming aware of it before that.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们在此之前就已经开始意识到这种现象了。

sentences.en: And many people who have it that don't have a mind's eye.
sentences.zh: 许多患有此症、没有“心灵之眼”的人……

sentences.en: First of all, when somebody makes a film of their favorite book and other people are complaining, oh, you know, this doesn't look how I expected.
sentences.zh: 首先，当有人把他们最喜欢的书拍成电影，而其他人都在抱怨，噢，你知道的，这跟我想象的不一样。

sentences.en: And they're going like, well, I didn't expect it to look like anything.
sentences.zh: 他们会想：嗯，我本来也没指望它长成什么样啊。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is that in their life, they have assumed that everybody's use of visual language with respect to memory is figurative.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在他们的生活中，他们一直以为所有人对记忆中视觉语言的使用都只是一种修辞。

sentences.en: And so they make that assumption.
sentences.zh: 所以他们便如此假设。

sentences.en: They don't actually, they think, oh, that's metaphorical.
sentences.zh: 他们其实并不……他们会想，哦，那是隐喻。

sentences.en: Well, they're figuratively speaking as if.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们只是在用比喻的方式说话。

sentences.en: But actually, they're actually having a very different experience.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们的体验大不相同。

sentences.en: They are genuinely not seeing anything.
sentences.zh: 他们真的什么也看不见。

sentences.en: Their memory and their perception, their imagination is organized fundamentally differently.
sentences.zh: 他们的记忆、感知和想象力的组织方式有着根本的不同。

sentences.en: And there's a whole sliding scale.
sentences.zh: 而且这里有一个完整的滑动量表。

sentences.en: It's not an on-off thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是非黑即白、非开即关的事情。

sentences.en: As developers, we like to think in terms of ones and zeros.
sentences.zh: 作为开发者，我们喜欢用一和零来思考问题。

sentences.en: No, it's not like that at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是这样的。

sentences.en: You get hyperphantasia at the other end of the scale, which is just like your memory, how you imagine things is super vivid, even beyond reality.
sentences.zh: 量表的另一端是超强幻象（hyperphantasia），也就是你的记忆以及你想象事物的方式极其生动，甚至超越了现实。

sentences.en: And so there's this kind of idea of there's a whole sensory experience that some people have got more of and other people are absolutely missing, which, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这就产生了一种概念，即某些人拥有更丰富的感官体验，而另一些人则完全缺失这种体验，你知道的，

sentences.en: whenever you're in a conversation where somebody has or has not got one of these things, there's always this kind of look of disbelief or, you know, what does that feel like?
sentences.zh: 每当你在交谈中遇到有人拥有或没有其中某项特质时，总会有一种难以置信的表情，或者会问：那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And it's just like what it feels like being is one of those things.
sentences.zh: 这就好比“存在”的感觉就是其中之一。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it's an interesting one, aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 不过，说真的，心盲症确实是一个很有趣的现象。

sentences.en: Yeah, we've talked about this now a couple of times over the last week.
sentences.zh: 是的，在过去的一个星期里，我们已经聊过好几次了。

sentences.en: And I had not, I didn't know the word aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 而且我以前并不知道“心盲症”这个词。

sentences.en: And you, we'll link it in the show notes, you sent me a podcast, I think it was, was it Rutherford and Fry?
sentences.zh: 你——我们在节目shownotes里会附上链接——你发给我一个播客，我想那是……是《卢瑟福与弗莱》（Rutherford and Fry）吗？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or is it, I got that backwards?
sentences.zh: 还是说，我记反了？

sentences.en: Anyways, it's a very interesting conversation.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，这是一场非常有趣的对话。

sentences.en: And yeah, the idea that you don't have a visualization in your head, like I took a quiz online.
sentences.zh: 是的，脑海中没有可视化画面的这种观点……就像我在网上做了一个测试。

sentences.en: It said that I had hyperphantasia, but I'm a little, I'm a little skeptical.
sentences.zh: 它说我有超强幻象，但我对此有点儿怀疑。

sentences.en: It was on some, like, you know, takeaquiz.org, so I, because I, I don't have the vividness, but I definitely, you know, I talk with my wife all the time about this, is that, like,
sentences.zh: 那是在某个诸如“来做个测试.org”之类的网站上测的，因为我……虽然我没有那种极致的生动感，但我绝对——我经常跟我妻子聊这个——

sentences.en: my ability to go back and replay, like, a run in my head from, like, you know, 10 years ago that I used to do, like, on a, you know, every second day.
sentences.zh: 我回想和重现脑海中画面的能力，比如十年前我经常做的那种跑步训练，每两天一次的那种。

sentences.en: Like, I can, there's a run that I used to do in China when I lived in Hangzhou.
sentences.zh: 就像我可以，我以前住在中国杭州时，有一条经常跑的路线。

sentences.en: I can still visualize, like, all the turns.
sentences.zh: 我依然能把所有的拐弯处在脑海中可视化出来。

sentences.en: It's not, like, more than reality, but, like, when I ask her, oh, like, don't you remember we just went on a drive?
sentences.zh: 虽然没有现实那么夸张，但当我问她：“噢，难道你不记得我们刚刚开车兜风了吗？”

sentences.en: And she's like, I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 她就会说：“我完全没印象。”

sentences.en: And then the same thing you mentioned, textures.
sentences.zh: 还有你刚才提到的质感，也是一样。

sentences.en: We've always talked about how we think that our palates are on, like, a different experience level because a lot of stuff, I think her distribution or range, it's like, ah,
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论，我们觉得彼此的味觉处于不同的体验层级，因为很多东西，我猜她的味觉分布或范围是这样的：啊，

sentences.en: everything's kind of good.
sentences.zh: 什么东西都差不多挺好吃的。

sentences.en: Where I'm just like, ah, if there's cheese in something, it is, I can, I could smell it on the speaker dinner we had the other night.
sentences.zh: 而我则是那种：啊，如果这里面有奶酪，我是……在前几天那场演讲嘉宾晚宴上，我一闻就能闻出来。

sentences.en: And they had the risotto that they put down.
sentences.zh: 他们端上了意式烩饭。

sentences.en: And I could, before they even put it on the table, I could smell that there was cheese.
sentences.zh: 甚至在端上桌之前，我就能闻到里面有奶酪的味道。

sentences.en: Anyways, I just think it's very interesting because how often, except for this past week,
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我只是觉得这非常有趣，因为除了过去这一周，

sentences.en: are you ever really talking about the difference or the delta between you and your peers or your friends or your partners, how you experience the world?
sentences.zh: 你什么时候才会真正去讨论你与同龄人、朋友或伴侣之间，在体验世界的方式上存在的差异或微小差距呢？

sentences.en: Because kind of people, they say, oh, you're a bit odd for not liking cheese at the, you know, the extremity that, you know, it's like, well, if you could feel the reaction of,
sentences.zh: 因为人们总会说：“你因为不喜欢奶酪而表现得有点古怪，达到了那种夸张的程度。”你知道的，“这就好比，如果你能感受到那种反应，

sentences.en: like, what it's, it's, I mean, it doesn't seem that unreasonable.
sentences.zh: 就像……嗯，这似乎并非不可理喻。”

sentences.en: But I think for other people, they don't like something, it's like, ah, I just, I kind of prefer not to, but I can eat it.
sentences.zh: 但我想对其他人来说，当他们不喜欢某种东西时，他们会说：“啊，我只是……我个人倾向于不吃，但我其实也能吃。”

sentences.en: Anyways, and you said you've had discussions with your son about this stuff.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，你曾说你跟儿子讨论过这些事情。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what's illuminated, but obviously you discovered this in your 20s with a synesthesia, but talking to your son.
sentences.zh: 正是这些讨论带来了启发，当然你是在二十多岁时通过联觉发现了这一点，但跟儿子交流也是契机。

sentences.en: Anyways, it's, I'm not sure if you want to add, like, anything, but it's, I just think it's such a fundamental, like, the way we perceive the world.
sentences.zh: 总之，我不知道你是否想补充点什么，但我只是觉得这是个非常根本的问题，关乎我们如何感知世界。

sentences.en: Yeah, we, yeah, we, I will add that I, I used that in a, in a talk a few years ago, one that you've seen that, you know, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们……我们会补充一点，我几年前在一场演讲中用到过这个——你肯定看过那场——“你到底是什么意思？”

sentences.en: Where I kind of explored this idea of, like, some things there are common myths that when we communicate, and certainly in the world of software, we're always communicating,
sentences.zh: 我在那场演讲中探讨了这样一种观点：当我们在交流时，存在一些常见的误区，而且在软件领域，我们无时无刻不在交流，

sentences.en: we're trying to build stuff, we're trying to communicate what we mean.
sentences.zh: 我们试图构建东西，试图传达我们的真实意图。

sentences.en: And there's some things that we kind of typically get right, there's things that we know we often stumble over and therefore need to clarify, we're kind of aware of this.
sentences.zh: 有些事情我们通常能处理好，有些事情我们知道自己经常跌跟头，因此需要澄清，我们对此是有所察觉的。

sentences.en: And then there's stuff we don't even know we're assuming that is different.
sentences.zh: 但还有一些事情，我们甚至不知道自己正抱着完全不同的假设。

sentences.en: And, you know, I use this in a talk, basically saying here is this sliding scale of, you know, misunderstanding, but also shared experience to unshared experience.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我在演讲中用到了这个观点，基本上是说这里存在一个从误解，到共享经验再到未共享经验的滑动量表。

sentences.en: So it's genuinely hard when you have a particular experience, either because you have something heightened, something added, or something removed, what does that feel like?
sentences.zh: 所以，当你拥有某种特殊的体验时，确实很难向别人描述——无论是由于某种感官能力增强、新增了什么，还是去除了什么，那到底是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And it's really difficult to describe, but we often don't have a shared conversation.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难描述，但我们往往缺乏共同的对话语境。

sentences.en: So we don't know, we make assumptions about other people.
sentences.zh: 因此我们不得而知，并且会对其他人做出各种假设。

sentences.en: And that's, and I think that's a really interesting one that is just like, you know, listen carefully, listen, listen carefully, watch carefully.
sentences.zh: 而我认为，这是一个非常有趣的观点，就像是：仔细倾听，倾听，仔细倾听，仔细观察。

sentences.en: It's, it's a lot of what we want to do is much more careful observation, if you like.
sentences.zh: 我们要做的很多事情，如果可以的话，其实就是更仔细的观察。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, that made me just think, because the robot that I am, you know, I had to learn empathy at some point in my life, because it didn't come natural to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了一点，因为我本身是个机器人，你知道的，我不得不在人生某个阶段学会共情，因为这对我来说并非天生就会的。

sentences.en: And I read a couple different books that were all terrible.
sentences.zh: 我读了几本完全看不下去的不同书籍。

sentences.en: And they always had their basic, you know, summary was like, you know, empathy is about putting yourself in someone else's shoes.
sentences.zh: 它们的中心思想，你知道的，基本上总结起来就是，同理心就是设身处地为他人着想。

sentences.en: And that's not, for the longest time, I never really got that.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，我一直不太明白这一点。

sentences.en: I was like, I can put myself in their shoes.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，我完全可以设身处地为他们着想啊。

sentences.en: And it's like, yeah, it's not a, it's not a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，这其实没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: Like, well, why are you upset?
sentences.zh: 比如，你到底在难过什么？

sentences.en: But then I heard a quote that was, empathy is not actually putting yourself in someone else's shoes.
sentences.zh: 但后来我听到了一句话，同理心其实并不是把自己放在别人的鞋子里。

sentences.en: It's understanding what it's like for that person to be in their shoes.
sentences.zh: 而是去理解那个人处在自己的处境中是怎样一种感受。

sentences.en: Because when you put yourself in someone else's shoes, you bring your own lived experiences and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 因为当你把自己放在别人的位置时，你会带入你自己的生活经历等等。

sentences.en: And so, it's like, you go in their shoes, and then now you're just you again.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，你走进了他们的鞋子，然后现在你又变成了你自己。

sentences.en: And it's like, well, you know, I still think it's kind of, but if you actually think, well, what is it like for that person to be in their shoes?
sentences.zh: 这就好比，你知道的，我还是觉得这有点，但如果你真的去想，那个人身处自己的境地到底是什么感受？

sentences.en: And if you don't have a lived experience or anything that's remotely close to what they're going through,
sentences.zh: 如果你没有任何生活经历，或者没有任何与他们正在经历的事情哪怕有一点点相似的经历，

sentences.en: it is very hard to empathize because you now have to basically imagine what it is like for them with their, like, history and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 要产生同理心是非常难的，因为你现在必须基本上凭空想象他们带着各自的历史背景等经历时是怎样的感受。

sentences.en: And that is a, that can be a very difficult thing if you have, you know, the closer you are to having been through that, the much easier.
sentences.zh: 这是一件，这可能是一件非常困难的事，你知道的，你越是接近经历过那种事，就会容易得多。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, you know, I've gone through something very similar.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，哦，你知道的，我经历过非常类似的事情。

sentences.en: I completely empathize, you know, because I've been through it.
sentences.zh: 我完全能感同身受，你知道的，因为我经历过。

sentences.en: But if you haven't, anyways, it's another interesting, like, how experiences and perception, it's all, probably, we would all be living in a healthier,
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有经历过，不管怎样，这又是另一个有趣的话题，比如经历和感知是如何运作的，可能如果我们可以找到某种方式进行更多这样的对话，

sentences.en: better world if we could find a way to have more of these conversations.
sentences.zh: 我们大家都会生活在一个更健康、更美好的世界里。

sentences.en: And, anyways, and also, too, we learned, or I learned, because when I was listening to that podcast, they talk about aphantasia,
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，还有，我们了解到，或者说我了解到，因为当我听那个播客时，他们谈到了失认症，

sentences.en: but then they also talk about a lack of an inner monologue.
sentences.zh: 但接着他们也谈到了缺乏内心的独白。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, why is there, there's a word for synesthesia, aphantasia, but there's no word.
sentences.zh: 我就想，为什么会这样，联觉有专有名词，失认症也有，但为什么没有那个词呢。

sentences.en: There is a word for it, and it's anendophagia.
sentences.zh: 其实是有这个词的，叫做无内语症（anendophagia）。

sentences.en: Anendophagia.
sentences.zh: 无内语症。

sentences.en: Is that, and how do you pronounce it?
sentences.zh: 是这样的吗，这个词该怎么读？

sentences.en: I'm going to go with anendophagia, but it could be different.
sentences.zh: 我打算读作 anendophagia，但也可能会有别的读法。

sentences.en: So, if there are any, any neurologists or psychiatrists who are listening in, just let us know.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有任何神经学家或精神病学家在收听的话，请告诉我们一声。

sentences.en: But, yeah, another, I used to talk to my dad about that, because he was a massive reader as a kid, loved, like, consumed all of Robert Heimlein and all the sci-fi and Asimov,
sentences.zh: 不过，说到这个，我以前常跟我爸聊起这个，因为他小时候是个狂热的读者，非常喜欢、可以说是吞读了罗伯特·海因莱因以及所有的科幻小说和阿西莫夫，

sentences.en: et cetera.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: And I remember he said he talked to a, I can't remember if he was a teacher or a peer when he was in high school.
sentences.zh: 我记得他说过，他高中时曾跟一个人聊过，我记不清那是他的老师还是同龄人。

sentences.en: And he said he lived most of his life, like, inside of his head, just talking, you know, it's like that, in your monologue, you talk,
sentences.zh: 他说他生命中的大部分时间，都仿佛生活在自己的脑海里，一直在说话，你知道的，就像那样，在你的内心独白中，你在说话，

sentences.en: the person you talk to the most is that voice inside your head.
sentences.zh: 你说话最多的人就是你脑海里的那个声音。

sentences.en: And he said he met someone and said, oh, that kind of sounds crazy, like, I don't have a voice in my head.
sentences.zh: 他说他遇到过一个人，那人说，哦，这听起来有点疯狂，我脑海里可没有声音。

sentences.en: He was like, what?
sentences.zh: 他当时就想，什么？

sentences.en: Do people not have voices in their head?
sentences.zh: 难道人们脑海里没有声音吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there is this comment, and you probably come across this meme, there is this, you know, picture of Morgan Freeman, and then there is a quote,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以有这样一个评论，你可能也见过这个梗，有一张摩根·弗里曼的照片，旁边配了一段话，

sentences.en: and you are hearing him in your head, reading it.
sentences.zh: 然后你在脑海里听到他读这段话的声音。

sentences.en: Morgan Freeman, that's a very distinctive voice.
sentences.zh: 摩根·弗里曼，那是一个非常有辨识度的声音。

sentences.en: And the whole point there is that that is not true for everyone.
sentences.zh: 而这里的重点是，并非对所有人来说都是这样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but when, if somebody, and that notion, when you have an email from somebody that you know, you hear,
sentences.zh: 对，但是当，如果有人，这种观念，当你收到一封你认识的人发来的电子邮件时，你会听到，

sentences.en: it's different from an email from somebody who is anonymous and unknown to you, because you can hear their voice saying it.
sentences.zh: 这和来自匿名且你不认识的人的电子邮件是不同的，因为你能听到他们的声音在读着它。

sentences.en: It turns out that is not true for everybody.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这并不适用于所有人。

sentences.en: And more importantly, it's more true for some people than others.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，这对某些人来说比对其他人更真实。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I wonder, too, how many listeners, because we, I mean, it's over the first month or two, I think there's usually about 4,000 to 5,000 people that listen.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也在想，会有多少听众，因为我们，我是说，在头一两个月里，通常大概有4,000到5,000人收听。

sentences.en: There's got to be, just statistically speaking, a number of folks that are resonating with this.
sentences.zh: 仅从统计学上讲，肯定会有相当一部分人对此产生共鸣。

sentences.en: I wonder how many, though, are hearing it for the first time, you know?
sentences.zh: 不过我在想，有多少人是第一次听到这个，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like, I imagine of the people that have synesthesia, aphantasia, and endophagia, and maybe there's even a term for the way you experience different textures,
sentences.zh: 就像，我猜那些患有联觉、失认症、无内语症的人，或许甚至还有用来形容你体验不同质感的方式的术语，

sentences.en: are for the first time listening and being like, wait, what?
sentences.zh: 他们是第一次收听，然后心想，等等，什么？

sentences.en: Like, you know, I'm not alone, or like, I thought, or I didn't realize that people are, people are seeing, you know, pictures in their head, or they have a voice inside their head.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，我不是一个人，或者说，我以为，或者我没有意识到人们，人们能在脑海里看到图片，或者他们脑海里有一个声音。

sentences.en: Anyways, interesting food for thought.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，这真是个耐人寻味的思考素材。

sentences.en: Hopefully this causes some discussions, you know, go and talk to your coworkers or your partner or your family, and, yeah, make the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 希望这能引发一些讨论，你知道的，去和你的同事、伴侣或家人聊聊，然后，是的，让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: How many minutes we're at?
sentences.zh: 我们录了多少分钟了？

sentences.en: Oh, we're only halfway, so perfect.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们才进行到一半，太完美了。

sentences.en: Let's pivot to, because I'm eager to talk about, we'll talk a bit about the Yow talk afterwards.
sentences.zh: 让我们转换一下话题，因为我很急着谈谈，我们待会儿会聊聊 Yow 的演讲。

sentences.en: But so, I did not see Kevlin's second most recent, or technically, is it your more recent?
sentences.zh: 不过，我还没看凯夫林倒数第二个，或者严格来说，这是你最近的那个吗？

sentences.en: What's the talk that you gave for the first time most recently?
sentences.zh: 你最近一次第一次做的演讲是什么？

sentences.en: Was it the Copenhagen one?
sentences.zh: 是哥本哈根的那场吗？

sentences.en: That's a little bit of hard math to do, because...
sentences.zh: 这有点难算，因为……

sentences.en: I think it is the Copenhagen one.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是哥本哈根那场。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it is the Copenhagen one.
sentences.zh: 对，我想就是哥本哈根那场。

sentences.en: I'm trying to think.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: But certainly, that one was new.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，那场是全新的。

sentences.en: There was no previous version of it, and there has been no version since, and that was the beginning of October.
sentences.zh: 它之前没有过任何版本，之后也没有过其他版本，那是十月初的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it was the beginning of October, and it didn't hit YouTube.
sentences.zh: 对，那是十月初，而且当时还没上 YouTube。

sentences.en: It said when I watched it, which was on the plane when we were on our way to Brisbane, so a couple days ago.
sentences.zh: 我观看的时候，正是我们在去布里斯班的飞机上，也就是几天前。

sentences.en: And when I downloaded it from YouTube to watch it on the plane, it said it had dropped three weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 当我从 YouTube 下载它以便在飞机上观看时，上面显示它是三周前发布的。

sentences.en: So it, I think, was released sometime late November, and I was on my honeymoon then, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以它大概是在十一月下旬发布的，我想那时我正在度蜜月。

sentences.en: So, I usually, YouTube, very good at recommending me all of Kevlin's talks, even when there's, like, three views on it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我通常，YouTube 非常擅长向我推荐凯夫林的所有演讲，哪怕只有三个观看量。

sentences.en: It knows, huh?
sentences.zh: 它懂的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a Kevlin talk.
sentences.zh: 这是凯夫林的演讲。

sentences.en: Connor wants to watch this.
sentences.zh: 康纳想看这个。

sentences.en: And so, I was shocked to hear that there was a talk of yours that had come online, and I hadn't seen it.
sentences.zh: 所以，听说你有一场演讲上线了我却没看过，我感到很震惊。

sentences.en: And, actually, I'm going to guess the title.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实上，我要猜一下标题。

sentences.en: The Future That Was?
sentences.zh: 《过去的未来》（The Future That Was）？

sentences.en: Close.
sentences.zh: 接近了。

sentences.en: Close.
sentences.zh: 接近了。

sentences.en: The Way The Future Was.
sentences.zh: 《曾经的未来》（The Way The Future Was）。

sentences.en: The Way The Future Was.
sentences.zh: 《曾经的未来》（The Way The Future Was）。

sentences.en: And I'll hand the mic to you, and, yeah, feel free to spoil it for the listener.
sentences.zh: 现在我把话筒交给你，然后，是的，请随意向听众剧透一下。

sentences.en: We'll link it in the show notes, as we mentioned.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所提到的，我们会在节目简介中附上链接。

sentences.en: But tell them what this talk was about, and then we'll chat a little bit about it after you've told the listener.
sentences.zh: 但请告诉大家这个演讲是关于什么的，等你告诉听众之后，我们再稍微聊一聊。

sentences.en: Yeah, so this was a talk I did jointly with James Lewis from ThoughtWorks.
sentences.zh: 好的，这是我和 ThoughtWorks 的詹姆斯·刘易斯（James Lewis）共同完成的一场演讲。

sentences.en: We've been angling to do a talk together for probably about the last three years.
sentences.zh: 我们大概在过去三年里一直都在寻找机会合作一场演讲。

sentences.en: I did an interview with James about three years ago, and we just kind of nerded out on a whole bunch of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我大约三年前对詹姆斯进行过一次采访，当时我们只是就一大堆事情进行了极客式的畅聊。

sentences.en: And afterwards, we also continued talking, and have done so in various conferences and airports,
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我们也一直在交流，在各种会议和机场都聊过，

sentences.en: sometimes about science fiction, sometimes about politics, sometimes about the way the future was, in the sense of this difference that we'd noticed.
sentences.zh: 有时聊科幻小说，有时聊政治，有时聊曾经的未来，也就是我们注意到的这种差异感。

sentences.en: We're kind of a similar generation.
sentences.zh: 我们算是差不多同一代人。

sentences.en: And there was this notion, it started happening in terms of online meeting.
sentences.zh: 而且有这样一种观念，它开始以在线会议的形式出现。

sentences.en: We were both program committee members of the GoToConference.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都是 GoTo 会议的节目委员会成员。

sentences.en: And during each online meeting, James and I would sometimes end up talking about, oh, yeah, yeah, and this was an imagined thing back in the 1970s or 80s.
sentences.zh: 在每次在线会议期间，我和詹姆斯有时最后都会聊到，哦，对对，这是 20 世纪 70 年代或 80 年代人们想象中的事物。

sentences.en: People would project this into the future.
sentences.zh: 人们会将这些投射到未来。

sentences.en: And we also started talking about this idea that qualitatively is something that I'd noticed a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还开始谈论这样一个概念，从性质上讲，这是我几年前就注意到的。

sentences.en: It was first brought to my attention accidentally by my oldest son.
sentences.zh: 它最初是由我的大儿子无意中引起我的注意的。

sentences.en: I showed him a couple of books that I read as a kid, and these books were published in the late 70s.
sentences.zh: 我给他看了几本我小时候读过的书，这些书出版于 20 世纪 70 年代末。

sentences.en: And he was about the same age as I was then, so I guess he was around 10, 11.
sentences.zh: 他当时和当年的我年龄差不多，所以我想他大概 10 岁、11 岁左右。

sentences.en: And these are books of the future.
sentences.zh: 这些都是关于未来的书。

sentences.en: It turns out I have a few of these.
sentences.zh: 事实证明我还有几本这样的书。

sentences.en: These are quite popular.
sentences.zh: 这些书相当受欢迎。

sentences.en: But these particular ones, they got recompiled recently and re-released, the Usborne book of the future.
sentences.zh: 但其中这几本最近被重新汇编并重新发行了，也就是《尤斯伯恩未来之书》（The Usborne Book of the Future）。

sentences.en: It's a lovely piece of repackaging because what they've done is they haven't changed the original text.
sentences.zh: 这是一件很棒的重新包装作品，因为他们没有修改原文。

sentences.en: They've taken the original three slender volumes, put them in one, and said, the Usborne book of the future, just basically given it a tagline.
sentences.zh: 他们把原来三本薄薄的书合为一本，并命名为《尤斯伯恩未来之书》，基本上就是加了一个副标题。

sentences.en: This is how the 21st century looked from the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 这就是 20 世纪 70 年代眼中的 21 世纪。

sentences.en: Lovely way of repackaging the material, but also allowing me to have a version that is currently not falling apart.
sentences.zh: 这是一种重新包装材料的绝佳方式，同时也让我拥有了一个目前不会散架的版本。

sentences.en: And I got given that for Christmas, a couple of Christmases back.
sentences.zh: 那是前年圣诞节时别人送给我的圣诞礼物。

sentences.en: But when my son was younger, he looked at these books, and he was just absolutely fascinated.
sentences.zh: 但当我的儿子更小的时候，他看着这些书，简直着迷了。

sentences.en: He was just looking at these books and going like, why don't we have anything like this now?
sentences.zh: 他只是看着这些书，然后说，为什么我们现在没有这样那样的东西了？

sentences.en: And I suddenly thought, oh, that's kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 我突然想，哦，这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: And if you like, this talk was a response to that question.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，这场演讲就是对这个问题的回应。

sentences.en: I mean, I apologize to my son.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我要向我的儿子道歉。

sentences.en: The response is nearly a decade and a half late.
sentences.zh: 这个回应迟到了近一个半 A 纪（注：此处口误/夸张，意指迟到了很久）。

sentences.en: But the point there was it's exploring that question.
sentences.zh: 但重点在于它是对那个问题的探讨。

sentences.en: Why is this the case?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: What is so different about now?
sentences.zh: 现在的不同之处究竟在哪里？

sentences.en: Because there is the standard thing, you know, old man going like, yeah, it's not the way it used to be.
sentences.zh: 因为存在那种老派的套路，你知道的，老头子在那儿说，唉，现在不如从前了。

sentences.en: So I check, is that just me or is it an objective thing?
sentences.zh: 所以我去核实了一下，这只是我个人的感觉，还是一个客观事实？

sentences.en: And it turns out that it seems to be more of an objective thing.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，这似乎更多是一个客观事实。

sentences.en: And it's not just my son noticing an absence of books in that space.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是我儿子注意到那个领域缺乏书籍。

sentences.en: There are a few books that are published, but let's put it this way.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些书出版，但我们这么说吧。

sentences.en: They are not the same, not with the same kind of like optimism or prevalence that we used to have.
sentences.zh: 它们已经不一样了，不再带有我们过去那种乐观情绪或普及度了。

sentences.en: They were much more, there was a, if you like, there's a naive optimism at one level.
sentences.zh: 它们要多得多，如果你愿意的话，在某种程度上带有一种天真的乐观主义。

sentences.en: But there was also an idea that goes back.
sentences.zh: 但其中也包含着一种延续至今的理念。

sentences.en: Like, typically we find it within science fiction, but certainly post Second World War, an idea, a very strong idea of techno-optimism.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们通常在科幻小说中发现这一点，但二战后绝对有一种非常强烈的技术乐观主义理念。

sentences.en: Techno-optimism still exists, but I want to say that it was more, it was more of a default.
sentences.zh: 技术乐观主义现在依然存在，但我想说的是，它过去更多，过去更像是一种默认设定。

sentences.en: It was the idea that the future means progress.
sentences.zh: 那就是“未来意味着进步”的观念。

sentences.en: The 21st century is somehow, if we can just get past this small issue of maybe wiping ourselves out,
sentences.zh: 21 世纪某种程度上，如果我们能克服自我毁灭这个小问题，

sentences.en: if we can get past that, then the 21st century, maybe we grow up, it's a kind of a Star Trek universe.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能克服这一点，那么在 21 世纪，也许我们长大了，那会是一个类似《星际迷航》的宇宙。

sentences.en: It's like we get to a point and all of the potential is unleashed, all of these possibilities.
sentences.zh: 就像我们达到了某个节点，所有的潜力都被释放出来，所有的可能性都被打开。

sentences.en: And this is not just sort of saying, you know, flying cars and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是指那种飞天汽车之类的东西。

sentences.en: It's much deeper in terms of like thinking about utopias and along those lines.
sentences.zh: 在思考乌托邦以及诸如此类的事情方面，它要深刻得多。

sentences.en: And there was genuinely a sense in the 70s and 80s, I can't speak for the 60s, I was not really there, only vaguely present.
sentences.zh: 在 70 年代和 80 年代确实有一种真切的感觉，60 年代我不敢说，我当时不在场，只是模模糊糊地存在着。

sentences.en: But 50s and 60s, you know, the Jetson view of the future, and you just see it in the science fiction of the time.
sentences.zh: 但在 50 年代和 60 年代，你知道的，《杰逊一家》对未来的展望，你在当时的科幻小说中随处可见。

sentences.en: Now, that continued, and then the 90s happened.
sentences.zh: 这种状态一直持续着，然后 90 年代降临了。

sentences.en: The Berlin Wall came down.
sentences.zh: 柏林墙倒塌了。

sentences.en: The Cold War was over.
sentences.zh: 冷战结束了。

sentences.en: We've done it.
sentences.zh: 我们成功了。

sentences.en: We've grown up.
sentences.zh: 我们长大了。

sentences.en: You know, this is all good.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这一切都很好。

sentences.en: And there is this whole idea, I mean, this is actually a quote in the talk that I used, Darren Aronofsky.
sentences.zh: 而且这里面有整个概念，我的意思是，这实际上是我在演讲中引用达伦·阿罗诺夫斯基（Darren Aronofsky）的一句话。

sentences.en: It's just like the 90s, you know, it was just like wonderful period where we didn't have the threat of nuclear destruction of the whole race.
sentences.zh: 就像 90 年代，你知道的，那是一个美妙的时期，我们没有全人类面临核毁灭的威胁。

sentences.en: The worst political scandal was Bill Clinton having an affair.
sentences.zh: 最大的政治丑闻就是比尔·克林顿有了婚外情。

sentences.en: You know, that was it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就这事。

sentences.en: And it was just like the 21st century is filled with possibility.
sentences.zh: 而且当时感觉 21 世纪充满了无限可能。

sentences.en: We've arrived.
sentences.zh: 我们已经抵达了。

sentences.en: We're about to get it.
sentences.zh: 我们就要得到了。

sentences.en: We're on the edge.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于边缘。

sentences.en: Yeah, we are on the edge.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们正处在边缘。

sentences.en: All the good stuff is like, oh, the web.
sentences.zh: 所有好东西都像，哦，万维网。

sentences.en: So the network, you know, the online network you saw referred to in so much science fiction, this is all good.
sentences.zh: 所以网络，你知道的，你在那么多科幻小说中看到的在线网络，这一切都很好。

sentences.en: You know, there was just a sense of wealth disparity.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时人们有一种感觉，财富差距。

sentences.en: That's not going to be a problem.
sentences.zh: 那将不再是个问题。

sentences.en: The future is going to be filled with all these kinds of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 未来将会充满各种各样的可能。

sentences.en: Anyway, 21st century arrived, and that apparently is not where we're at.
sentences.zh: 总之，21世纪已经到来，而我们显然并没有身处那种未来。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, things changed.
sentences.zh: 因此，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: You can put it in a kind of post-9-11 era kind of view.
sentences.zh: 你可以从一种类似“9·11”事件之后的视角来看待它。

sentences.en: There's lots of different things.
sentences.zh: 有很多不同的事物。

sentences.en: But there was something qualitatively different about people's perspectives.
sentences.zh: 但人们的看法有着本质上的不同。

sentences.en: And, again, checking through age groups that there is a difference here.
sentences.zh: 而且，再次审视各个年龄段，会发现这里确实存在差异。

sentences.en: In 2025, when we look at 2050, it doesn't feel – it doesn't have the same feeling as being in 1975 looking at 2000.
sentences.zh: 在2025年，当我们展望2050年时，这种感觉——它与1975年展望2000年的感觉完全不同。

sentences.en: We do have a – let's be very clear.
sentences.zh: 我们确实——让我们把话说清楚。

sentences.en: We have some really cool stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些非常酷的东西。

sentences.en: And, actually, in the talk, we break the talk down into a number of sections.
sentences.zh: 而且，实际上，在演讲中，我们把演讲分成了几个部分。

sentences.en: The way the future was, and then the title of the talk, and then the way the future is, which is slightly more depressing, when we compare it.
sentences.zh: 过去的那种未来，接着是演讲的标题，然后是现在的那种未来，当我们进行比较时，它显得稍微有些压抑。

sentences.en: And the way the future came to be, where we actually look at what's the mechanics of stuff.
sentences.zh: 以及未来是如何变成这样的，在这一部分我们实际上探讨了事物的运作机制。

sentences.en: And that's a little more interesting.
sentences.zh: 这要有趣一些。

sentences.en: And then we basically end with the way the future could be, you know, if you like, a call to action.
sentences.zh: 然后我们基本上以未来可能会是什么样来结尾，你知道的，如果你愿意的话，这就像是一个行动呼吁。

sentences.en: But it's not a guarantee.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一个保证。

sentences.en: We're not guaranteed of anything.
sentences.zh: 我们对任何事情都没有绝对的保证。

sentences.en: So, by the way, plenty of spoilers here in this sense.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，从这个意义上说，这里有很多剧透。

sentences.en: But there is a comparative thing that in the 1970s there was a view – people like Gerard O'Neill were putting forward the idea of, like, hey, we can have cities in space.
sentences.zh: 但有一个对比点是，在20世纪70年代有一种观点——像杰拉德·奥尼尔这样的人当时提出了一种想法，比如，嘿，我们可以在太空中建造城市。

sentences.en: And he had a very particular view, and a lot of the imagery will be familiar to anybody who's watched science fiction filMs.
sentences.zh: 他有非常独特的观点，而且许多意象对于看过科幻电影的人来说会非常熟悉。

sentences.en: These have made their way in, vast orbital structures.
sentences.zh: 这些已经融入其中，比如庞大的轨道结构。

sentences.en: These have made their way into mainstream media.
sentences.zh: 这些已经进入了主流媒体。

sentences.en: But he had a very particular vision, and it was a very utopian one.
sentences.zh: 但他有一种非常独特的愿景，那是一个非常乌托邦式的愿景。

sentences.en: And then we get films like 2013's Elysium, which is a much darker, darker picture.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到了像2013年的《极乐空间》这样的电影，这是一幅黑暗得多的画面。

sentences.en: We have the beautiful orbital, but it's only for the top fraction of a percent.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有美丽的轨道空间站，但它只属于极少数的顶层富豪。

sentences.en: It is kind of the ultimate gated community.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是终极版的封闭式高档社区。

sentences.en: And it is the same physical structure, and yet the political and wealth disparity and the overtones that go with it are quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且它的物理结构是相同的，然而政治和财富的巨大差距以及伴随而来的弦外之音却相当有趣。

sentences.en: And I recently re-watched Elysium in 2025, and it's a very different experience to watching it in 2025.
sentences.zh: 我最近在2025年重看了《极乐空间》，这与在2025年观看它的体验截然不同。

sentences.en: In that kind of post-2016 world, there's a lot that's been – a lot of things that are kind of like, oh, dear, this is not the future we had hoped for.
sentences.zh: 在那种2016年之后的世道中，有很多事情——很多事情都让人觉得，天哪，这并不是我们曾希望拥有的未来。

sentences.en: There's still a lot of things that are possible, but when we look at the possibilities, this is where we start painting a picture of optimism,
sentences.zh: 仍然有很多事情是可能的，但当我们审视这些可能性时，这正是我们开始描绘乐观图景的地方，

sentences.en: is that most things happen not because you try to make them.
sentences.zh: 那就是大多数事情的发生并不是因为你刻意去尝试实现它们。

sentences.en: In other words, the video phone – people spent the better part of the 20th century trying to make video phones, and it never took off.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，可视电话——人们花了20世纪的大部分时间试图制造可视电话，但它从未真正流行起来。

sentences.en: And it turns out the video phone, when it happened, it happened just not because people were trying to create a video phone.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，可视电话当它真正出现时，并不是因为人们当时正试图创造可视电话。

sentences.en: It was incidental.
sentences.zh: 那是个意外。

sentences.en: It relied on other technologies.
sentences.zh: 它依赖于其他技术。

sentences.en: It had a prevalence that came from messaging platforMs.
sentences.zh: 它的普及度源自消息传递平台。

sentences.en: In other words, it was not from the – you know, in the 20th century, it was people like AT&T.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它并不是源于——你知道的，在20世纪，是像美国电话电报公司（AT&T）这样的人。

sentences.en: They were kind of exploring video phones, and of course they would because they're a telecommunications company.
sentences.zh: 他们当时在某种程度上探索可视电话，当然他们会这么做，因为他们是一家电信公司。

sentences.en: But the video phone did not come from the telecoms companies.
sentences.zh: 但可视电话并不是由电信公司带来的。

sentences.en: It came through kind of the back door of like a communications backplane that was ubiquitous, sufficient bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 它是通过某种“后门”走进现实的，也就是那种无处不在、拥有足够带宽的通信骨干网。

sentences.en: The fact that sometimes people wanted to extend their messaging, whether that was, you know, MS Messenger or whether that was, you know, more recently WhatsApp,
sentences.zh: 有时人们希望扩展其消息功能，无论是微软的MS Messenger，还是你懂的，最近的WhatsApp，

sentences.en: you notice that all of these have a secondary video facility.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到所有这些都有一个辅助的视频功能。

sentences.en: It's just like tacked on because you could have it.
sentences.zh: 它就像是顺便附加上去的，因为你完全可以拥有它。

sentences.en: And that's the whole point.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: It made it inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这让它变得不可避免。

sentences.en: And we see that – so we see that kind of idea that the way to get certain technologies is not by targeting the technologies but by looking at what they are built on.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这一点——所以我们看到了这样一种观点：获得某些技术的途径不是通过把目标锁定在技术本身，而是通过审视它们所构建的基础。

sentences.en: And that gives a very, very different picture.
sentences.zh: 这展现出了一幅非常非常不同的图景。

sentences.en: We have a lot of conversations about the car.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多关于汽车的讨论。

sentences.en: People love using car metaphors.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢使用汽车隐喻。

sentences.en: And everybody focuses on the technology of the car.
sentences.zh: 每个人都把焦点放在汽车的技术上。

sentences.en: But the biggest boon to the car was the tarmac road.
sentences.zh: 但对汽车最大的恩赐却是柏油路。

sentences.en: Without that, the modern car would not look like it does.
sentences.zh: 如果没有它，现代汽车就不会是现在的样子。

sentences.en: It would not have its ubiquity.
sentences.zh: 它也不会有如此高的普及度。

sentences.en: Cities would not look like they do.
sentences.zh: 城市也不会是现在这个样子。

sentences.en: It turns out that it was the road that made the car.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，是道路造就了汽车。

sentences.en: Of course, the car was – just like my devices have to have a camera for me to have a video experience.
sentences.zh: 当然，汽车——就像我的设备必须配备摄像头我才能获得视频体验一样。

sentences.en: You have to have a car to have a driving experience.
sentences.zh: 你必须得有一辆车才能有驾驶体验。

sentences.en: But actually, the biggest contributor to its social uptake is the road and how we think about roads and how we organize roads.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，对其社会普及贡献最大的是道路，以及我们如何看待道路和组织道路。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, as technologists, the trick is we kind of keep aiming, sometimes a little bit too high,
sentences.zh: 因此，作为技术人员，这里的诀窍在于我们的目标有时定得有点太高了，

sentences.en: and then being disappointed by the failure of adoption, only to see it happen a decade later when some other technology,
sentences.zh: 然后又因未能被大众采纳而感到失望，结果却发现在十年后，当某种其他技术、

sentences.en: some other platform-level thing or something that becomes hidden but ubiquitous becomes normal.
sentences.zh: 某种平台级别的东西或某种变得隐形却无处不在的东西成为常态时，它才真正实现了普及。

sentences.en: So, James and I kind of explore a number of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，詹姆斯和我探讨了其中许多事情。

sentences.en: We talk in terms of, like, energy distribution.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了能量分配之类的话题。

sentences.en: We talk about the failure of the metaverse.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了元宇宙的失败。

sentences.en: It's a kind of retro-futurist idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一种复古未来主义的想法。

sentences.en: It's like what people thought the future might look like in the 1980s and early 90s.
sentences.zh: 就像人们在20世纪80年代和90年代初对未来样子的想象。

sentences.en: But we arrived at a different version of the web.
sentences.zh: 但我们迎来了不同版本的网络。

sentences.en: Our experience is fundamentally different.
sentences.zh: 我们的体验有着根本的不同。

sentences.en: I don't want to be walking through a virtual shopping mall in order to buy stuff.
sentences.zh: 我可不想为了买东西而逛虚拟购物中心。

sentences.en: That's a janky, slow experience.
sentences.zh: 那是一种蹩脚而缓慢的体验。

sentences.en: Why would I want to do that when, with a flick of a couple of keystrokes, I can order stuff immediately?
sentences.zh: 既然只要敲几下键盘就能立刻下单，我为什么还要去做那种事？

sentences.en: We ended up with a catalogue metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我们最终采用了目录隐喻。

sentences.en: So, you know, online shopping is an extension of the catalogue metaphor.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，网上购物是目录隐喻的延伸。

sentences.en: It is not an extension of the shopping mall experience.
sentences.zh: 它并不是购物中心体验的延伸。

sentences.en: And we've already made that decision.
sentences.zh: 我们已经做出了那种选择。

sentences.en: And so there's this interesting thing that there's a future that was, a future path not taken.
sentences.zh: 所以这就产生了一个有趣的现象：曾经存在过一个未来，一条未曾选择的未来之路。

sentences.en: So we kind of talk a little bit about that.
sentences.zh: 因此我们对此做了一些讨论。

sentences.en: But that notion of the optimism, the, you know, we stored a lot of hope up.
sentences.zh: 但那种乐观主义的概念，你知道的，我们积蓄了大量的希望。

sentences.en: We lived under a particular, well, we lived under a particular shadow of the atom.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在特定的、嗯，我们生活在原子能的特定阴影之下。

sentences.en: We also had post-Second World War optimism.
sentences.zh: 我们还拥有二战后的乐观主义。

sentences.en: We talk a little bit more about other culture perspectives in the talk as well.
sentences.zh: 我们在演讲中也稍微讨论了其他文化的视角。

sentences.en: But there is this idea that in the 21st century, something else has happened.
sentences.zh: 但有一种观点认为，在21世纪，发生了别的事情。

sentences.en: We've achieved a dominance.
sentences.zh: 我们取得了一种统治地位。

sentences.en: The tech bro dominance is, it turns out that they're not all in it for the good things.
sentences.zh: 科技界大佬们的统治地位，结果证明他们并不完全是为了好事而来。

sentences.en: They're not in it for the good of humanity.
sentences.zh: 他们不是为了人类的福祉而来的。

sentences.en: And it turns out that with great power, you can exercise any kind of lack of responsibility you want.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，拥有巨大的权力，你就可以肆意妄为地不负任何责任。

sentences.en: And that becomes the, that becomes part of the issue.
sentences.zh: 这便成了，这便成了问题的一部分。

sentences.en: But at the same time, that's also our call to action at the end of the talk.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，这也是我们演讲最后的行动呼吁。

sentences.en: We kind of like, you know what, this could be different.
sentences.zh: 我们有点像在说，你知道吗，这一切本可以不同。

sentences.en: We have an immense amount of power collectively.
sentences.zh: 我们集体拥有巨大的力量。

sentences.en: Most of the technologies for solving real problems have not yet been put together.
sentences.zh: 大多数用于解决实际问题的技术尚未被组合在一起。

sentences.en: But they are there.
sentences.zh: 但它们就在那里。

sentences.en: They're waiting to be done.
sentences.zh: 它们正等待着被付诸实践。

sentences.en: So there is possibility there.
sentences.zh: 所以那里存在着可能性。

sentences.en: But we, yeah, it was an interesting exploration.
sentences.zh: 不过我们，是的，这是一次有趣的探索。

sentences.en: But the bit I loved most about the talk, in addition to doing the talk, getting the chance to do it with James,
sentences.zh: 但我最喜欢这次演讲的部分，除了做这场演讲本身、有机会和詹姆斯一起完成它、

sentences.en: having a really receptive audience, answering the question that my son laid out, was also, it allows me to do a non-code or software-related talk.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个非常积极回应的观众、回答我儿子提出的问题之外，还在于它允许我做一个与代码或软件无关的演讲。

sentences.en: So technically, I'm now a futurologiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以严格来说，我现在是一名未来学家了。

sentences.en: You know, I could be completely wrong, but most futurologists are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可能会完全猜错，但大多数未来学家都是如此。

sentences.en: So that's not, that does not discredit me from that.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不会、这并不会因此而贬低我的资格。

sentences.en: But I can now put that on my CV.
sentences.zh: 但我现在可以把这个写进我的简历里了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the reason the talk came up was because we were talking about a conversation that had been had at the first instance in Melbourne.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这个演讲之所以会出现，是因为我们在讨论最初在墨尔本进行的一次对话。

sentences.en: And I realized that I had accidentally become like the bad guy, like the tech bro.
sentences.zh: 我意识到自己不小心变成了那种坏人，就像科技界大佬一样。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I talk with Shima, my wife, all the time, and that she always tells me that I'm a techno-optimist, transhumaniSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，我是说，我经常和我的妻子希玛交谈，她总是告诉我我是一个技术乐观主义者、超人类主义者。

sentences.en: And then after this conversation, I went and talked with her.
sentences.zh: 在这场对话之后，我去找她聊了聊。

sentences.en: And she was like, you know about the Overton window, which I was like, ah, I've heard of it.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道俄车因窗（奥弗顿之窗）吗？我说，啊，我听说过。

sentences.en: Anyway, she sent me a diagram, and she's like, what you have to understand is you have like radical views that society is not ready to accept.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，她发给我一张图表，并说：你必须明白的是，你有一些社会尚未准备好接受的激进观点。

sentences.en: The interesting part, though, is that you're basically kind of in your talk show that like it used to not be radical to be hopeful about this technology.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，你在演讲中基本上表明，对这项技术抱有希望过去并不是一件激进的事。

sentences.en: But now because of the, you know, it's multifactorial, you know, the political climate, you know,
sentences.zh: 但现在由于种种，你知道的，这是多重因素导致的，你知道的，政治气候，你知道的，

sentences.en: the wealth inequality, you know, and it's like, and I had to really think about it.
sentences.zh: 财富不平等，你知道的，这让我不得不认真思考。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, wow, like saying that I want to chip in my wrist for all this, you know, future stuff.
sentences.zh: 这就好像是，哦，天哪，比如我说我想把芯片植入我的手腕来迎接所有这些，你知道的，未来的东西。

sentences.en: People, you know, and my wife, she even said that, oh, like, you know, that can be offensive to some people, you know.
sentences.zh: 人们，你知道的，我妻子甚至说过，哦，像，你知道的，这可能会冒犯某些人，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's like you're trying to take the humanity out of, and I was like, that's not what I'm trying to do.
sentences.zh: 这就像你试图剥夺其中的人性一样，而我说，那不是我试图做的。

sentences.en: I just, it's like the equivalent of you hovering cars and whatever for the future.
sentences.zh: 我只是，这就像是未来里你拥有会飞的汽车之类的东西的等同说法。

sentences.en: Anyways, I just think it's a great talk.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我只是觉得这是一个很棒的演讲。

sentences.en: People should watch.
sentences.zh: 人们应该去看看。

sentences.en: And it leads to interesting discussions of like, you know, it's not just Elysium, which is a fantastic film, but like I love anything adjacent to that.
sentences.zh: 它引出了有趣的讨论，比如，你知道的，不仅仅是《极乐空间》这部非常棒的电影，我还喜欢任何与之相关的作品。

sentences.en: Like, you know, Altered Carbon is a TV show based on a book.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，《碳变》是一部根据书籍改编的电视剧。

sentences.en: I've read the first book.
sentences.zh: 我读过第一本书。

sentences.en: The books are, even the show, I think, it's like PG-18 or R.
sentences.zh: 这些书，甚至这部剧，我认为，大约是限制级（PG-18或R级）。

sentences.en: So if you, we got young listeners, wait a few years until you're in university.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你，如果我们有年轻的听众，再等几年等你上了大学再看吧。

sentences.en: But, you know, like Black Mirror.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，就像《黑镜》一样。

sentences.en: And to be honest, a lot of the kind of future based shows are dystopic.
sentences.zh: 说实话，许多这类以未来为背景的剧集都是反乌托邦的。

sentences.en: You know, Alien, Sean Parent, a recent guest, he was talking about Alien and how the, they have the five,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，《异形》，肖恩·帕伦特，最近的一位嘉宾，他谈到了《异形》以及他们如何拥有这五个，

sentences.en: which are, it's a post-government society where five corporations govern the world, you know, not, not out of the realm of anyway.
sentences.zh: 也就是，这是一个后政府社会，由五家大公司统治着世界，你知道的，这并非完全不可能发生。

sentences.en: So it's interesting, though, that there aren't, there are way more dystopic kind of future TV shows versus like the Jetsons.
sentences.zh: 所以很有趣的是，反乌托邦式的未来美剧明显比像《杰逊一家》那样的剧要多得多。

sentences.en: We've got the vacuum cleaner robot.
sentences.zh: 我们有了扫地机器人。

sentences.en: It's very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不太确定。

sentences.en: Also, too, if listeners have recommendations of anything adjacent to Elysium, Altered Carbon, Black Mirror, any of that, I love that stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有，如果听众有什么关于《极乐空间》、《碳变》、《黑镜》或任何类似作品的推荐，我非常喜欢这些。

sentences.en: I'm always looking.
sentences.zh: 我一直在寻找。

sentences.zh: 《潘神》？（注：指动画《Pantheon》）

sentences.en: I guess Pantheon's an anime, depending on how that was recommended by Joao, a past guest on the pod.
sentences.zh: 我想《潘神》是一部动漫，具体取决于它是怎么被播客的上一位嘉宾若昂推荐的。

sentences.en: Or not this pod, but a RaycaSt.
sentences.zh: 或者不是这个播客，而是一个叫RaycaSt的节目。

sentences.en: Just, that's kind of not fully dystopic.
sentences.zh: 总之，那并不是完全的反乌托邦。

sentences.en: It's about becoming an uploaded intelligence so you can go through an operation and have your brain zapped and then you're living in the cloud.
sentences.zh: 它是关于变成上传的智能体，这样你就可以通过一次手术让你的大脑被扫描，然后你就能生活在云端了。

sentences.en: That's the transhumanism thing that doesn't sound all bad to me, folks.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个超人类主义的东西，听起来对我来说并不是全无坏处，各位。

sentences.en: I'm going to hand, Kevlin has something to.
sentences.zh: 我要把话筒交给凯夫林，他有话要说。

sentences.en: Oh, it's not about the transhumanism.
sentences.zh: 哦，这跟超人类主义无关。

sentences.en: It's just one of the things that we mentioned in the talk.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们在演讲中提到的事情之一。

sentences.en: I was just thinking in terms of the dystopianism is that dystopianism isn't new, but it had a different meaning in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我只是在思考反乌托邦主义，反乌托邦主义并不是什么新鲜事，但它在过去有不同的含义。

sentences.en: So, therefore, some of these same things taken out of context or put in a different context mean something different.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中一些相同的事情如果脱离上下文或者被放在不同的语境中，就会意味着不同的东西。

sentences.en: So, for example, historically, a lot of the stuff that we associate with a kind of a cyberpunk future, things like Altered Carbon,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，从历史上看，许多我们与某种赛博朋克未来相关的东西，比如《碳变》之类的事物，

sentences.en: if you go back to kind of Blade Runner and things like that, most of the ideas, although they did touch on certain possibilities of the future in terms of corporatism and politics,
sentences.zh: 如果你追溯到《银翼杀手》之类的内容，大多数想法虽然它们在企业化和政治方面触及了未来的某些可能性，

sentences.en: they were very, very gentle by comparison.
sentences.zh: 但相比之下，它们已经非常非常温和了。

sentences.en: They were mostly thematic.
sentences.zh: 它们大多是主题性质的。

sentences.en: So, in other words, a lot of the idea is like we're going to adopt this as a visualization, as a style, as a feel within the story.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，很多想法就像是我们要把这作为一种视觉化呈现、一种风格、一种故事中的氛围来采用。

sentences.en: Not necessarily – Alien Earth is actually quite a good example because you now have this – it's a fully-fledged idea of the dominance of corporations.
sentences.zh: 不一定——《异形：地球》其实是一个很好的例子，因为你现在拥有了这个——这是一个关于公司统治地位的完全成型的概念。

sentences.en: The original Alien didn't really have that.
sentences.zh: 最初的《异形》并没有真正展现这一点。

sentences.en: That's something that's emerged over time.
sentences.zh: 那是随着时间推移才逐渐显现出来的东西。

sentences.en: The corporate idea has just become a bigger, bigger thing, and we've kind of grown into it.
sentences.zh: 企业理念变得越来越庞大，我们算是顺应了这种发展。

sentences.en: We've got louder background music now, folks, so you'll probably still be able to hear us, but the audio quality may or may not have just declined.
sentences.zh: 各位，我们现在背景音乐声音变大了，所以你们大概还能听到我们说话，不过音频质量可能有所下降。

sentences.en: I'm not sure why that is necessary.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定为什么非得这样。

sentences.en: Anyways, it should be fine.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，应该没问题。

sentences.en: But, yes, go watch the talk.
sentences.zh: 但是，对，去看看那个演讲吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure we still have a day and a half left.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确信我们还有一个半天的时间。

sentences.en: I'm sure it'll get talked about some more.
sentences.zh: 我相信大家还会进一步讨论这件事。

sentences.en: But it is, I think, a very, very interesting conversation and, like, societally important, right?
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，这是一个非常非常有趣且对社会很重要的对话，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I am pretty sure, except for maybe a few of the billionaires out there, nobody wants to live in a world with, you know, income inequality skyrocketing
sentences.zh: 比如，我很确信，除了外面可能那几个亿万富翁之外，没有人想生活在一个贫富差距急剧扩大的世界里，你知道的，

sentences.en: and people being left behind because, you know, AI is a tool that half of society can take advantage of and the other half, it's just going to hurt their circumstances.
sentences.zh: 人们被时代抛弃，因为，你知道的，AI是一种一半人能受益、另一半人处境会因此受损的工具。

sentences.en: I think the majority of society can agree that we do not want that.
sentences.zh: 我想社会的大多数人都会同意我们不希望那样。

sentences.en: And, you know, talks like this start conversations and, you know, I had never really thought about the fact.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这样的谈话能引发讨论，而且，你知道，我以前从没真正想过这个事实。

sentences.en: You know, for the longest time, I just thought I was on the good side.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很长一段时间里，我都以为自己站在正义的一边。

sentences.en: You know, I always thought I was, I was about to say a Jedi, but then there's some people out there that have theories that the Jedi are actually the bad guys.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我一直以为我是，我本来想说我是个绝地武士，但外面有些人理论说绝地武士其实才是坏人。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if you got a take on that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你对此有什么看法。

sentences.zh: 凯夫林在布里斯班的第二版活动中穿了一件《星球大战》夏威夷衬衫。

sentences.zh: 如果你还没看，我待会儿发给你。

sentences.zh: 你看过那个吗？

sentences.zh: 因为我们一直在讨论《安多》，各位。

sentences.zh: 凯夫林，超级《安多》迷，超级星战迷。

sentences.zh: 你有什么想告诉大家的？

sentences.zh: 我对加加·宾克斯没有什么具体的看法，不过我曾经是“马切特顺序”的超级粉丝，基本上，如果你不熟悉那个，
